name: Brick-based structures
text:
# Brick-based structures
## Overview
Brick-based structures replace the variable-resolution hierarchical subdivision of sparse voxel octrees with fixed-size cubic blocks ("bricks") to optimize for hardware-friendly memory access and parallel construction [S1, unofficial]. They solve the traversal complexity and shader divergence of recursive [tree structures](#4139-tree-based-structures-octree-pointer-tree-sparse-voxel-dag.md) by enabling branch-free, linear memory access patterns suitable for real-time ray tracing and GPU cache coherency [G].
## Shared principles
The family partitions the 3D domain into fixed-granularity cubic blocks rather than recursive nodes [S1, unofficial]. These blocks are stored in a sparse container (e.g., a low-resolution grid or hash map) that maps spatial regions to brick data [G]. This approach prioritizes uniform granularity to balance memory usage and traversal speed, specifically optimizing for hardware interpolation and parallel processing [S1, unofficial].
## Subtopics

### [Sparse Voxel Brick Set](11886-sparse-voxel-brick-set.md)
Groups Signed Distance Field ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) data into fixed-size cubic blocks, each associated with a raytracing Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB). It balances memory efficiency and real-time constructibility, specifically optimizing for GPU cache coherency and parallel construction. Unlike Sparse Voxel Octrees (SVOs) which vary resolution, or Grid Sphere Tracing which stores every [voxel, the Brick](#5794-voxel-bricks.md) Set uses a uniform brick granularity to balance memory usage and traversal speed, making it particularly effective in complex scenes. Choose it when hardware-friendly memory access and parallel construction are prioritized over variable resolution.

### [Brick Map](21177-brick-map.md)
A two-level sparse spatial data structure for ray tracing that combines a low-resolution full voxel grid with high-resolution sparse 'bricks' to store triangle indices, avoiding the traversal complexity of BVHs and SVOs while skipping free space. It is designed specifically for real-time ray tracing of secondary rays (reflections/refractions) starting from surfaces, supporting dynamic content and allowing ray bouncing with controlled execution time. Unlike SVOs which require stack-based or recursive traversal, the [Brick Map](#21177-brick-map.md) allows hard-coded, branch-free traversal by always reading the low-resolution cell to determine if a brick is present, resulting in low shader divergence. Choose it for real-time secondary ray tracing with dynamic content where branch-free traversal is critical.

### Sparse Voxel Octree with 3x3 Bricks
Uses 3x3 voxels per [octree](#18524-octree.md) node corner for hardware interpolation [S1, unofficial]. Memory usage is less than half that of previous solutions [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of using small bricks within an [octree structure](#2792-octree-based-structures.md) for real-time indirect illumination was introduced by Crassin et al. in 2009 [S1, unofficial]. This approach was designed to avoid costly precomputation steps and allow dynamic updates for animated objects and dynamic modifications of the environment [S1, unofficial]. The technique utilizes hardware interpolation while significantly reducing memory usage compared to previous solutions [S1, unofficial].
## Sources
[S1] Interactive Indirect Illumination Using Voxel Cone Tracing: An Insight, https://openalex.org/W4296123939, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial)
